label: Retorsion: unrestricted characterization fails and contrary sole-God definitions clash
paraphrase: Four checked facts about definitional frames, analyst formulation. (a) In every frame the unrestricted characterization principle is logically false: a single instance, at an unsatisfiable description, fails. (b) In every frame, for any predicates 'God' and 'omnibenevolent', if 'the existing being that is the only God and is omnibenevolent' and 'the existing being that is the only God and is not omnibenevolent' have both been defined, then 'whatever is defined is true' is false: its contrary instances clash, since the two satisfiers would both be the only God, hence identical, and both omnibenevolent and not. (c) Each of the two descriptions is satisfied in some frame, so the clash does not come from a single self-contradictory description. (d) P1 and the weak P2 hold together in some frame (one object, only P1's description defined): they are jointly consistent. The predicates are arbitrary; the result is not about the God of the root.
